question: On Friday 1 March 2024, Energy Commissioner Simson delivered a speech at the inaugural session of the Southern Gas Corridor Advisory Council. In this speech, she congratulated President Aliyev of Azerbaijan with his re-election. She also called Azerbaijan a trusted partner and stated that the country has the European Union’s full support.

Parliament has recently and repeatedly expressed its concern1 about the human rights situation in Azerbaijan and the aggressive policies of the Azeri regime against Armenia, which have also led to the ethnic cleansing of the Nagorno-Karabakh region since September 2023. 1.

How do the statements of the Commissioner relate to the concerns of Parliament about the deplorable human rights situation in Azerbaijan and its aggressive policy towards Armenia and the people of Nagorno-Karabakh?
What signal is the Commission conveying to Armenia, which has been on the receiving end of the aggressive policies of the Aliyev regime for years?
Why does the Commission choose to seek rapprochement with Azerbaijan instead of suspending the Memorandum of Understanding on a Strategic Partnership in the Field of Energy with Azerbaijan?
answer: The EU has repeatedly called on Azerbaijan to adhere to their obligations under international law, reacting publicly concerning detentions of political opponents and journalists. The EU conveyed its position on the presidential elections of 7 February 2024 (2). The EU continues to engage with Azerbaijan as part of the regular human rights dialogue and bilaterally.

The EU called upon Azerbaijan to ensure the rights of Armenians in the Karabakh region, including their right to return to their homes without intimidation and discrimination. The EU reiterates that a violation of Armenia’s territorial integrity would have clear consequences on the EU-Azerbaijan bilateral relations.

At the same time, the EU remains committed to facilitating dialogue between Armenia and Azerbaijan to achieve a sustainable peace, also via the EU mission in Armenia. Cooperation with both countries is thus important and the energy sector offers many opportunities in this regard.

The Memorandum of Understanding on Energy (3) signed on 18 July 2022 with Azerbaijan is part of the EU’s efforts to diversify its energy sources and decrease dependence on Russia, in the context of which Azerbaijan has effectively been a trusted partner. Energy cooperation with Azerbaijan also reflects a shared ambition to accelerate the development and deployment of renewable energy production.

The EU calls on Azerbaijan to use the momentum of the annual United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP29) to step up its efforts towards reaching the objectives of the Paris Agreement (4). Cooperation in the field of energy does not influence the EU’s stance in the normalisation process between Armenia and Azerbaijan and is not done at the expense of the dialogue with Azerbaijan on human rights and democracy.
